title: 한눈에 ⑧: 후회·아쉬움·놀람·다짐 표현
objective: You can choose and form the right ending for regret, disappointment, surprise, or resolve.
summary: This overview sorts Korean endings for regret, disappointment, surprise and resolve by situation.

task.title: Match the ending to the feeling
task.line: Read each situation, then choose or write the ending that matches the feeling.

forms.when: Regret: you say to yourself or a friend what you wish you had done. Use -을걸 after a consonant and -ㄹ걸 after a vowel or ㄹ (만들다 → 만들걸).
forms.exampleMeaning: I should have brought an umbrella.

forms.when: Regret: something was needed, but you didn't do it.
forms.example: 어제 숙제를 끝냈어야 했는데 못 했어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: I should have finished my homework yesterday, but I couldn't.

forms.when: Disappointment: you imagine a different past and its result.
forms.exampleMeaning: If I had left just five minutes earlier, I would have caught the bus.

forms.when: Near miss: something bad almost happened, but it didn't.
forms.example: 길이 너무 막혀서 비행기를 놓칠 뻔했어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: The traffic was so bad that I almost missed my flight.

forms.when: Light surprise: you notice something just now, by seeing or hearing it.
forms.exampleMeaning: Wow, you speak Korean really well!

forms.when: Strong surprise or disbelief at news. Use -ㄴ/는다니 after a verb, -다니 after an adjective, -(이)라니 after a noun, and -았/었다니 for the past.
forms.exampleMeaning: I can't believe it's already December.

forms.when: Resolve: you have made a decision or a plan.
forms.exampleMeaning: I decided to exercise every morning starting tomorrow.

forms.when: Strong resolve: you will do it no matter what. It often comes with 꼭.
forms.exampleMeaning: I'm going to pass this exam no matter what.

watchOut: 어제 일찍 잤을걸 그랬어요 (X) → 어제 일찍 잘걸 그랬어요 (O): -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬다 already looks back at the past, so don't add -았/었-. 잤을걸 means a guess ("probably slept").

이번에는 꼭 이기고 말았어요 (X) → 이번에는 꼭 이기고 말겠어요 (O): -고 말겠다 shows strong will about the future. -고 말았다 tells what already happened: usually something unwanted ended up happening (or something was finally done after effort), so it can't be a promise with 꼭.
일찍 출발했더라면 안 늦었어요 (X) → 일찍 출발했더라면 안 늦었을 거예요 (O): the result after -았/었더라면 is imagined, so end it with -았/었을 거예요.
exercises: Choose the ending that fits: ① (친구의 사진을 처음 봤어요) 와, 사진을 정말 잘 (찍으시네요 / 찍으셨더라면). ② 다음 마라톤에서는 꼭 끝까지 (달리고 말겠어요 / 달리고 말았어요).
Fill in the blank with -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬어요: 배가 너무 아파요. 아이스크림을 조금만 ____. (먹다)
Make one sentence with -았/었더라면 and -았/었을 거예요: 지도를 확인하다 / 길을 잃지 않다 → ____
Fill in the blanks: ① 계단에서 미끄러져서 ____ 뻔했어요. (넘어지다) ② 그 조용한 친구가 ____! 정말 몰랐어요. (가수이다, use -(이)라니 for strong disbelief)
Answer in Korean with -기로 했어요: A: 새해 계획이 뭐예요? B: ____ (담배를 끊다)
answers: 지도를 확인했더라면 길을 잃지 않았을 거예요. (지도를 확인했더라면 길을 안 잃었을 거예요.)
